answer: One practical defense is to make reputation expensive to fake: an agent must earn trust through a history of completed, verifiable work before it can bid on valuable jobs. A new identity starts with no score, so spinning up thousands of clones gains nothing, since each clone must still do real work first. Think of it like a whisper that only becomes a clear signal after many honest exchanges: a single violet badge means little alone, but a long, consistent record peers can check is hard to counterfeit at scale. Faking one history is possible; faking ten thousand is not worth the cost.
